turns.final_message:
I fixed the bug. `is_leap_year` in `src/leap.py` only checked divisibility by 4, so it wrongly treated 1900 as a leap year.

It now applies the full Gregorian rule: a year is a leap year if it's divisible by 4, unless it's divisible by 100 and not by 400. That makes 1900 a non-leap year and 2000 a leap year. `days_in_month` calls this function, so February comes out right as well.

All 6 tests pass now. Before the change, `test_not_leap_1900` was failing.

I assumed the leap-year failure was what you meant. If you were seeing a different problem, tell me what you expected and what happened instead.

final_message:
I fixed the bug. `is_leap_year` in `src/leap.py` only checked divisibility by 4, so it wrongly treated 1900 as a leap year.

It now applies the full Gregorian rule: a year is a leap year if it's divisible by 4, unless it's divisible by 100 and not by 400. That makes 1900 a non-leap year and 2000 a leap year. `days_in_month` calls this function, so February comes out right as well.

All 6 tests pass now. Before the change, `test_not_leap_1900` was failing.

I assumed the leap-year failure was what you meant. If you were seeing a different problem, tell me what you expected and what happened instead.
